subject: maths
question: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 105 km in downstream and in coming back?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Time = Distance ÷ (Speed of Boat + Speed of Stream) + Distance ÷ (Speed of Boat − Speed of Stream)

Total Time = 105 ÷ (18 + 3) + 105 ÷ (18 − 3)

Total Time = 105 ÷ 21 + 105 ÷ 15

Total Time = 5 + 7 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (u) = 18 km/h

Speed of stream (v) = 3 km/h

Distance covered each way (D) = 105 km

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed (Dₛ) = u + v

Upstream Speed (Uₛ) = u − v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d1fd925dee30df94bba02ef01b3842b98a934d819db47bdc842c0a9e10a2025.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed (Dₛ) = 18 + 3 = 21 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (Uₛ) = 18 − 3 = 15 km/h

⇒ Time taken downstream = 105 ÷ 21 = 5 hours

⇒ Time taken upstream = 105 ÷ 15 = 7 hours

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 7 = 12 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat and Stream from Downstream / Upstream

If downstream speed is Dₛ and upstream speed is Uₛ, then Speed of Boat = (Dₛ + Uₛ) ÷ 2, and Speed of Stream = (Dₛ − Uₛ) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for a Round Trip

For a journey traveling the same distance downstream and upstream, Average Speed = (Dₛ × Uₛ) ÷ Speed of Boat in still water.

Total Time Formula

If total time for a round trip is T, then Total Distance = (T × (u² − v²)) ÷ (2 × u), where u is boat speed and v is stream speed.
